title: Introduce budgeted fallback strategy + compact-batcher v1
author: Ethan Cole
description:
Motivation: In production we saw bursts where cheaper quantized variants were saturated and naive fallbacks would either (a) switch immediately to high-cost variants or (b) reject requests -- both harming unit economics or availability. This PR implements a budgeted, gradual fallback policy tied to a compact-batcher that intentionally trades small latency increases for large unit-cost savings.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a budgeted fallback controller (src/runtime/fallback/budgeted_fallback.py) that tracks a short-term microbudget (token-cost budget) per-serving-group and applies a rampdown window before switching to a higher-cost model variant.
- Introduces compact-batcher v1 (src/runtime/batcher/compact_batcher.py) optimized for short sequences and mixed-quant model variants; supports size-aware packing and a leaky-token accounting hook used by the budget controller.
- New default profiles: config/default_profiles.yaml includes conservative "economy-first" presets and safety multipliers per-customer tier.
- Observability: adds metrics and alerting hooks (metrics/runtime/econ_fallbacks.md and dashboards/compact_batcher.jsonnet) to surface fallback rate, budget burn, and cost delta when fallbacks occur.
- Tests and e2e smoke: tests/test_compact_batcher.py and tests/test_budgeted_fallback.py with synthetic workloads and replay traces.

Checklist:
- [x] Budget controller implementation
- [x] Compact-batcher implementation + performance microbench
- [x] Backwards-compatible config patch
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: short playbook and rollout notes
- [x] CI green and staging rollout observed (2-day shadow)

Compatibility notes:
- Default behavior is opt-in via config flag "enable_budgeted_fallback". Existing customers are unaffected until profiles are promoted.
- Compact-batcher is registered behind the routing policy and will only be used for compatible model variants (mixed-quant / short-seq paths).

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: miscalibrated budgets could cause unnecessary degradation. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-customer multipliers, and a kill-switch to revert to immediate fallback behavior.
- Risk: batching regressions for long-sequence workloads. Mitigation: compact-batcher only triggers for sequences < 128 and includes a fallback to the existing batcher.

Release notes:
- Feature: Budgeted fallback controller and compact-batcher v1 (opt-in); adds economic fallback profiles and observability for fallback events.

Related: ENG-1649 (budgeted fallbacks design), ENG-1710 (compact-batcher spec).
